html:
The crossing of the Rhine frontier into Roman Gaul by a mixed host of Vandals, Alans and Suebi, traditionally dated 31 December 406. It probably happened near Mainz. Some historians place it a year earlier.

The Rhine had been one of the best guarded borders of the empire. But the general Stilicho had pulled troops back to defend Italy against the Goths, and the invaders met little resistance. They plundered Mainz, Trier and other cities across northern Gaul. Jerome, writing in Bethlehem, listed the ruined towns in a letter.

The army in Britain raised its own emperor, Constantine III, who took the last troops to Gaul; this helped bring the end of Roman rule in Britain. In 409 the invaders crossed the Pyrenees into Spain, and in 429 the Vandals went on to Africa. Rome never fully won back the west. The crossing is a key date of the Migration Period.
